obligations.text: A run's state is a fold over its run record alone: replaying the record reproduces every lease, operation outcome and attempt, and no operation state lives only in memory or in a capped table.

An operation whose idempotency key the record already holds for that run, with the same operation and version, appends nothing and answers the recorded outcome; the same key with a different operation or version is refused as key-conflict.
An operation whose expected version is not the run's current version is refused with exit 2 and the closed reason stale-version, and appends a refusal, never the effect.

An operation submitted without the run's current lease is refused with exit 2 and the closed reason lease-not-held, before any idempotency or version rule of section 3.3, so a caller without the lease learns nothing about keys.
An abort records stop-requested when it is accepted and stop-confirmed only when the attempt's cancelled outcome is durable; neither is read as the other.

A record built by a sequence of operations replays to the same state; a repeated key appends nothing; a stale version exits 2 naming stale-version; a reconnecting cursor reads exactly the events after it.

sectionHeadings: 048: Typed run operations under one controller lease
record.summary: Gives a run three typed operations, attempt.retry, attempt.continue and attempt.abort, submitted by one controller holding a lease. Each carries an idempotency key and the run version it was decided against; each request and its outcome append to spec 003's hash-linked run record, durable and uncapped, so replaying the record reproduces the run's state. A reconnecting controller reads events from a cursor over the record. The one live slot of spec 003 section 3.7 is held or released explicitly by each operation.
record.title: Typed run operations under one controller lease, recorded in the run record
